manifest.name: dsh-effort-router
manifest.description: DSH plugin: context-aware per-step reasoning-effort routing (the drift engine). Classifies the task origin once (trivial/standard/engineering/hard) from the originating brief, then drifts the class on stacked evidence: a decay-weighted short window of tool errors / repeats / todo completions / orchestration returns / compaction checkpoints / failure carry, a long window of gzip-discounted information volume on linear ramps, and real-time frugal signals — no hysteresis. Clamps to the target model's advertised efforts and injects an 'Auto' mask into the native model selector. Fills default reasoningEfforts for profile-declared llm-pi-ai custom models the Models page has not configured (0.2.1-aware). All user-facing options live in the plugin config file (no settings UI); the GUI surfaces (composer badge, trajectory hoisting) are read-only displays.
manifest.author: moonshotai-kimi-k3, moonshotai-kimi-k3.1-pro, deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 (AI co-authors), produced by KEI.NEO (@neo805)

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**Version:** `0.2.16-rc.2` (DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 compatible) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Roadmap](ROADMAP.md)

A DSH (DeepSeek Harness) plugin: **context-aware per-step reasoning-effort routing**, plus reasoning levels for hand-declared `llm-pi-ai` custom models.

- **The drift engine** (0.2.8; integer ranks since 0.2.16): the task ORIGIN CLASS is classified once from the brief the user sent (`trivial / standard / engineering / hard`); `routes` maps it to an integer origin rank, then evidence drifts the **rank** — `targetRank = originRank + error channel + volume channel − frugal`, clamped to the hard-anchor ceiling
- Error channel (short 6-step window, decay-weighted): tool errors, identical-argument retries, event bumps (a just-completed todo, an orchestration return, a compaction checkpoint — each +1 once per step), and a carry from the previous task's unresolved failure
- Volume channel (long 32-step window): brief and tool-result tokens, **gzip-ratio discounted** (repetition is not information), graded by two linear ramps
- Warm-up floor: a fresh task never routes below its origin for the first steps (default 3); afterwards drift owns the level — aggressive saving, with the short error window as the feedback loop
- Wish detector: a short delegation-style brief in the cue vacuum zone (`帮我…`, `can you…`) starts at the engineering floor — underspecified tasks get the benefit of the doubt
- Frugal signals: subagents, context pressure, or a

readme.section: Why an Auto mask instead of a panel
readme.text: The host's native model selector already is the per-session effort control. The plugin advertises an `Auto` level on every reasoning-capable model (injected into `reasoning.efforts`, resolved to a concrete wire level by the request interceptor before validation), so there is **no second selector to keep in sync**: Auto schedules, a concrete level passes through.

**Since DSH 0.2.1 the Models page can declare reasoning levels per custom model in the UI** (a switch plus one row per level), so editing the config file is no longer required. The plugin's auto-fill therefore narrows to **models declared in the profile layer that the settings user layer has never touched**: once a model appears in the user layer (edited in the UI) it is treated as user-owned — the UI's switch stores OFF by REMOVING the field, so re-filling it would silently undo that choice, and the fill skips it. Catalog models that already inherit levels resolve WITH levels and are skipped, so catalog capability is never shadowed; an explicit table or an explicit `false` is never touched. The filled table is `{ low, high, max }`, deliberately with **no `off` rung**: an off selection followed by a tool call poisons the conversation for every later thinking-enabled request, and the router never routes to off either. Models filled on explicit `openai-completions` routes also gain `compat.supportsReasoningEffort: true`, the switch that protocol needs to actually send the effort. Set `fillCustomModels: false` to let the Models page own every declaration. A profile-declared model that

The per-model level → gateway wire-value mapping (e.g. `high → ultra`) lives in the model's `reasoningEfforts` table inside the `llm-pi-ai` config — edit it directly or ask your agent to. The official schema validates it and the next request picks it up. pi-ai serializes the table natively; no plugin-side translation layer.

readme.section: Configuration (no settings UI — everything lives in the config file)
readme.text: **The plugin deliberately ships NO settings UI** (since 0.2.7-rc.6): every user-facing option lives in the plugin configuration, stored on the profile side, so **upgrading the plugin package never overwrites it**. Change options by editing the config or by asking your agent in natural language ("hide the badge", "allow max").

readme.section: Configuration (no settings UI — everything lives in the config file)
readme.text:
- `enabled`: master switch (off = requests pass through untouched)
- `defaultLevel`: level when nothing is selected (`auto` or a concrete level)
- `subagentEffort`: subagent default (`inherit` or a concrete level)
- `allowedEfforts`: optional global final selector-id allow-list (`minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultra`); empty = every advertised non-off level. `off/none/auto` are reserved and rejected
- `effortFallback`: missing-target behaviour — `nearest-up` (compatibility default), `up`, or `down`; directional modes clamp at the available boundary
- `allowMax` / `maxFallback`: **deprecated in 0.2.16**. `allowMax=false` migrates to an `allowedEfforts` ceiling up to `maxFallback`; setting both old and new controls is reported as a conflict
- `wish` / `poisonRecovery` / `frugalDemote` / `contextPressure` / `sessionTokenBudget`: wish detector, poison recovery, frugal demotion and their thresholds
- `showBadge`: show the read-only badge left of the composer model selector (default on)
- `trajectoryAnnotate`: project each step's `provider/model · effort` onto the native trajectory ledger (default on; switch off if it conflicts with another plugin)
- `chatAnnotate`: add a `provider/mo

- **Composer badge** (left of the model selector, gated by `showBadge`): the mode and **actually sent** effort of the session's last step (`Auto · high`); the tooltip carries origin class, target tier/rank, mapping mode, and reason. Read-only — control stays in the native selector.
- **Trajectory hoisting** (`trajectoryAnnotate`, default on): each step's `provider/model · effort` is projected onto the NATIVE trajectory ledger rows (DOM projection anchored on `data-trajectory-row-key` — the assembly-layer route, no host package touched and no new view added). The anchor table is folded host-side from `request/header` + `assistant/message` + `tool/call` events and served on the state route. Session identity comes from the conversation root's `data-conversation-session` (0.2.11): a switch blanks the old captions and repaints from the new session's table, and an unknown identity paints nothing rather than a neighbouring session's capsule. The chat flow itself stays annotation-free by default.
- **Chat captions** (`chatAnnotate`, **default off**): when enabled, each tool call gains a `provider/model · effort` caption row fed by the same anchor projection.

- The interceptor is one try/catch: any error passes a concrete request through untouched; the plugin's virtual `Auto` sentinel is stripped even on that path (fail-open without leaking Auto)
- Models without reasoning metadata never receive `reasoningEffort` — never an `UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT`
- Automatic routing never emits `off` (thinking continuity on strict thinking-mode APIs). A history PROVEN poisoned — a reasoning-less tool-call turn exists AND the session's decision log recorded a manual `off` step — pins `off` with a warning until compaction removes the offending turn. Shape alone never pins: models like kimi-K3 emit no reasoning blocks before tool calls with thinking on (measured, 2026-10-10). Disable via `poisonRecovery` if your routes are all non-strict
- Session reads go through `deriveMessages()` + `sessionProjections` only; an empty sample raises an explicit warning instead of silently degrading
